blocks.instruction: Leia o texto e escolha a alternativa correta. Algumas perguntas pedem inferência — a resposta não está escrita com todas as letras.
blocks.passage:
Culture is not the poster on the wall with the company values. Culture is what actually happens in the room when the poster is not there. It is the sum of the small behaviours that managers and employees accept or reject every day.

A strong culture is built slowly, through rituals, stories and decisions. Who gets promoted? Who gets fired? Which behaviours are rewarded in public? These are the real signals, and every employee reads them instantly, even if HR never writes them down.

Culture is fragile. It takes years to build and months to lose. When a company grows fast, or merges with another, culture is often the first casualty — unless leaders actively protect it.

items.q: According to the text, where does culture really show itself?
options: On the poster with the company values
In what happens when the poster is not there
items.why: "Culture is what actually happens in the room when the poster is not there."

items.q: What does the text say the 'real signals' of culture are?
options: The size of the office and its layout
Who gets promoted, fired or rewarded in public
The number of company events per year
items.why: "Who gets promoted? Who gets fired? Which behaviours are rewarded in public? These are the real signals."

items.q: The phrase "years to build and months to lose" suggests that culture is…
options: only a concern for large companies
items.why: Inferência: construir leva muito mais tempo do que perder — logo é frágil e o dano não se recupera na mesma velocidade.

items.q: Which statement would the author most likely DISAGREE with?
options: Employees read cultural signals even when they are unwritten.
A promotion sends a message about what the company values.
Writing values on the wall is enough to create a strong culture.
A merger can put a company's culture at risk.
items.why: Inferência: o texto todo argumenta que cultura é comportamento, não pôster — a frase contradiz a tese.

items.q: The phrase "unless leaders actively protect it" implies that…
options: protecting culture is the job of HR alone
leaders have little influence over culture
culture survives on its own during fast growth
without deliberate effort, growth or mergers can damage culture
items.why: Inferência: a cultura é a primeira vítima do crescimento ou fusão a menos que haja esforço deliberado da liderança.

blocks.instruction: Ouça Sophie abrindo o workshop de cultura depois da fusão. Responda sem ler a transcrição — ela só aparece depois de corrigir.

audio.text:
Good morning, everyone. Before we start, let me be honest about why we are in this room. Two companies have just become one on paper — but on paper is the easy part. Today we are here to decide how we actually work together.

I want to be clear about one thing. We are not going to spend the day rewriting a list of values and printing it on a nice poster. The poster is not the culture. The culture is what you do on a Tuesday afternoon, when nobody is watching and there is a difficult decision to make.

So here is how we will spend the morning. First, each team tells one real story — a moment that made you proud of how your old company behaved. Then we look for the rituals behind those stories, because rituals are what keep a culture alive when the founders have gone.

And I will say this plainly: the fastest way to destroy trust after a merger is to reward, in public, the behaviour that half the room quietly rejects. So watch who we promote in the next six months. That, not this workshop, is the real message.
audio.label: Ouça quantas vezes precisar. A transcrição aparece depois de corrigir.

items.q: Why does Sophie say the two companies are together on paper but the hard part remains?
options: The offices have not merged yet
Deciding how they actually work together is the real challenge
The legal documents are not finished
The new logo has not been chosen
items.why: "on paper is the easy part. Today we are here to decide how we actually work together."

items.q: According to Sophie, when does culture really reveal itself?
options: When the new poster is printed
On a Tuesday afternoon, facing a difficult decision unwatched
items.why: "The culture is what you do on a Tuesday afternoon, when nobody is watching and there is a difficult decision to make."

items.q: Why does Sophie ask each team to tell a real story first?
options: To find the rituals that keep a culture alive
To decide which company was better
To choose a new company name
items.why: "we look for the rituals behind those stories, because rituals are what keep a culture alive."

items.q: What does Sophie imply is the 'real message' after a merger?
options: Who gets promoted over the next six months
The new list of printed values
The size of the merger deal
items.why: Inferência: "watch who we promote… That, not this workshop, is the real message."

items.q: How would you best describe Sophie's approach in the talk?
options: Ceremonial and focused on the poster
Vague and undecided about the plan
Direct and sceptical of symbolic gestures
items.why: Inferência: ela é franca ("let me be honest", "I will say this plainly") e desdenha do pôster em favor do comportamento real.

blocks.instruction: O vocabulário da lição aparece aqui em frases novas. Escolha o sentido ou a palavra que cabe no contexto.

items.q: "Every Friday demo is a small ritual that reminds the team who they are." A ritual is…
options: a repeated practice that carries shared meaning
a one-off event that never repeats
items.why: Ritual = prática repetida com significado compartilhado, que sustenta a cultura.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "If we celebrate results but quietly ___ the behaviour behind them, people notice the contradiction."
items.why: Reject = rejeitar; o contraste com "celebrate" pede o oposto de recompensar.

items.q: "Constant reorganisation slowly eroded the trust the team had built." To erode means to…
items.why: Erode = corroer, desgastar aos poucos.

items.q: "After the merger, two ways of working suddenly had to share one office." A merger is…
options: the launch of a new product
the hiring of a new leadership team
the combining of two companies into one
items.why: Merger = fusão: duas empresas que se tornam uma.

items.q: "The CEO apologised first — a clear example of tone at the top." This phrase refers to…
options: the top floor of the building
the highest salary in the company
the example that senior leaders set for everyone
items.why: Tone at the top = o exemplo dado pela liderança, que orienta o comportamento de todos.

blocks.instruction: Expressões que aparecem em conversas sobre cultura e fusões. Escolha o sentido no contexto.

items.q: "Leadership needs to live up to the values it prints on the wall." To live up to means to…
items.why: Live up to = corresponder, estar à altura de um padrão ou expectativa.

items.q: "After the merger, the two teams slowly bought into the new way of working." They…
options: came to accept and support it
items.why: Buy into = comprar a ideia, aderir e apoiar.

items.q: "A few managers pushed back on promoting someone who ignored the values." They…
items.why: Push back on = resistir, discordar de algo.

items.q: "If we don't follow through on the culture we describe, no one will believe it." To follow through means to…
items.why: Follow through = levar até o fim aquilo que foi prometido.

items.q: "One toxic senior hire can set the tone for a whole department." To set the tone means to…
options: establish the mood or standard others follow
items.why: Set the tone = definir o clima ou o padrão que os outros passam a seguir.
